                           NEW YORK STATE SENATE





                          THE STENOGRAPHIC RECORD









                             ALBANY, NEW YORK

                               May 12, 2003

                                 3:07 p.m.





                              REGULAR SESSION







            LT. GOVERNOR MARY O. DONOHUE, President

            STEVEN M. BOGGESS, Secretary















                                                        2449



                           P R O C E E D I N G S

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The Senate will

                 please come to order.

                            I ask everyone present to please

                 rise and repeat with me the Pledge of

                 Allegiance.

                            (Whereupon, the assemblage recited

                 the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

                 clergy, may we bow our heads in a moment of

                 silence, please.

                 respected a moment of silence.)

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Reading of the

                 Journal.

                 Friday, May 9, the Senate met pursuant to

                 adjournment.  The Journal of Thursday, May 8,

                 was read and approved.  On motion, Senate

                 adjourned.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Without

                 objection, the Journal stands approved as

                 read.

                            Presentation of petitions.

                            Messages from the Assembly.



                                                        2450



                            Messages from the Governor.

                            Reports of standing committees.

                            Reports of select committees.

                            Communications and reports from

                 state officers.

                            Motions and resolutions.

                            Senator Bruno.

                            SENATOR BRUNO:    Madam President,

                 I believe there's a privileged resolution at

                 the desk.  I would ask that it be read in its

                 entirety and move for its immediate adoption.

                            And I would ask the

                 Sergeant-at-Arms to call the members to the

                 chamber.  Could we do that?

                            Thank you, Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The Secretary

                 will read.

                            THE SECRETARY:    By Senator Bruno,

                 Legislative Resolution Number 1581, honoring

                 Funny Cide, the first New York-bred horse to

                 capture the illustrious Kentucky Derby.

                            "WHEREAS, on May 3, 2003,

                 New York-bred Funny Cide captured the 129th

                 running of the Kentucky Derby, the first leg

                 of horse racing's Triple Crown, at Churchill



                                                        2451



                 Downs in Louisville, Kentucky; and

                            "WHEREAS, Funny Cide, ridden by

                 jockey Jose Santos and trained by Barclay

                 Tagg, covered the mile and a quarter in a time

                 of 2:01.19 to win the "Run for the Roses" by a

                 length and three quarters in one of the ten

                 fastest times; and

                            "WHEREAS, Funny Cide also became

                 the first gelding to win the Derby since Clyde

                 Van Dusen in 1929.  In addition, the victory

                 gave both New York-based jockey Jose Santos

                 and his agent, Mike Sellitto, their first

                 Derby victory, along with New York-based

                 trainer Barclay Tagg; and

                            "WHEREAS, Funny Cide, by Distorted

                 Humor out of the Slewacide mare Belle's Good

                 Cide, was born at McMahon of Saratoga

                 Thoroughbreds, LLC, owned by Joseph and Anne

                 McMahon; and

                            "WHEREAS, Voted the New York-bred

                 Champion Juvenile Male for 2002, Funny Cide is

                 owned by Sackatoga Stables, which is managed

                 by Jackson Knowlton and comprised of Gus

                 Williams, David Mahan, Lew Titterton, Eric

                 Dattner, Jon Constance, Harold Cring, Mark



                                                        2452



                 Phillips, Peter Phillips, and Larry Reinhardt,

                 a group of former high school friends from

                 Sackets Harbor, New York, and two other

                 partners from the Capital Region; and

                            "WHEREAS, Along the road to

                 victory, Funny Cide was guided by assistant

                 trainer and exercise rider Robin Smullen,

                 groom Zacarias Quintana and hot walker Raunie

                 Hart; and

                            "WHEREAS, Undefeated in three

                 starts as a two-year-old, this tough, swift,

                 versatile competitor always seems to put forth

                 his best effort and is a worthy representative

                 of those qualities that are most appealing

                 among New York-breds; and

                            "WHEREAS, The accomplishments of

                 Funny Cide, the New York Thoroughbred

                 Breeder's, Inc., under the able leadership of

                 President Gerald A. Nielsen and Executive

                 Director Dennis J. Brida, and the New York

                 State Thoroughbred Breeding and Development

                 Fund Corporation, under the competent

                 direction of Chairman William A. Levin and

                 Executive Director Martin G. Kinsella, have

                 raised New York breeding to a new level of



                                                        2453



                 achievement; and

                            "WHEREAS, It is fitting and proper

                 for this Legislative Body to take note of such

                 a prestigious sporting event which brings

                 great pride not only to thoroughbred Funny

                 Cide and his proud owners, but to the horse

                 racing industry and all the citizens of this

                 great Empire State; now, therefore, be it

                            "RESOLVED, That this Legislative

                 Body pause in its deliberations to honor Funny

                 Cide, the first New York-bred horse to capture

                 the illustrious Kentucky Derby, and to extend

                 our best wishes on the quest for the Triple

                 Crown; and be it further

                            "RESOLVED, that copies of this

                 resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted

                 to Jose Santos, Barclay Tagg, Mike Sellitto,

                 Joseph and Anne McMahon, Jackson Knowlton,

                 Gus Williams, David Mahan, Lew Titterton, Eric

                 Dattner, Jon Constance, Harold Cring, Mark

                 Phillips, Peter Phillips, Larry Reinhardt,

                 Robin Smullen, Zacarias Quintana, Raunie Hart,

                 the Board of Directors of the New York

                 Thoroughbred Breeders, Inc., and the New York

                 State Thoroughbred Breeding and Development



                                                        2454



                 Fund Corporation."

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Bruno.

                            SENATOR BRUNO:    Thank you,

                 Madam President and colleagues.

                            Funny Cide, in 2:01.19, did for

                 New York State breeding what we in the

                 Legislature and the governors have tried to do

                 for decades:  put us on the map, made us

                 winners, made us champions.

                            And Barclay and Robin, the

                 trainers, who found him when he was young and

                 kept their eyes on him and bought him for the

                 owners, for the team headed up by Jack

                 Knowlton.

                            Jack worked here in the Senate.  He

                 got his training here in the Senate to have a

                 good eye and a keen mind, with Senator Marchi,

                 who is the longest-serving legislator in all

                 of the United States, and then went on in

                 business in Saratoga.

                            And Funny Cide is now my most

                 famous constituent.

                            (Laughter.)

                            SENATOR BRUNO:    Lives in the 43rd

                 District most of the time, at Joe and Anne



                                                        2455



                 McMahon's breeding ranch and farm.

                            And Joe and Anne went into business

                 some 31 years ago, something like that, and

                 really are pioneers here in the state, and did

                 it the hard way, to build a breeding program

                 and a breeding farm, which just takes a lot of

                 know-how, hard work, persistence, endurance,

                 all the good things.

                            So what a team.  And Rita Santos is

                 here, with four beautiful children -- where's

                 Rita? -- with the four beautiful children.

                 Jose had to be in California, straightening

                 out the record for history that he is a

                 winner, he is a champion, and Funny Cide truly

                 is a champion and worthy to be the lead, the

                 first time ever for a New York-bred to win the

                 Derby.

                            Jose Santos, first time ever to win

                 the Derby.  Barclay Tagg and Robin, first time

                 ever to win the Derby.

                            Jack, I don't think you've ever had

                 a Derby winner before -- no, in that team.

                            (Laughter.)

                            SENATOR BRUNO:    But you know

                 what?  Truly, I get very excited when I think



                                                        2456



                 about the controversy over the breed back rule

                 when we were funding the breeding program here

                 in New York State.

                            We have done, we together --

                 together here in the Senate, in the Assembly,

                 with the Governor -- some great things, not

                 for just the people of New York State, the

                 40,000 people that work in breeding and

                 agriculture, the 40,000 acres that are in

                 breeding farms throughout New York State, the

                 $6.5 million that was paid out in 2002 to

                 breeders for New York awards.

                            All of those good things have

                 happened with people having faith, having

                 confidence, recognizing that New York State,

                 working together, everybody in the industry --

                 trainers, breeders -- everyone that works out

                 there, legislators, business, investors, just

                 partnering together to move New York State

                 into the forefront in racing and in breeding

                 in the world.

                            So I am as proud as I can be to

                 congratulate everyone that has been involved

                 in getting us to this momentous occasion.

                            And the Preakness is this Saturday.



                                                        2457



                 And I doubt that the odds will be 12 to 1.

                            (Laughter.)

                            SENATOR BRUNO:    You think so?  I

                 have a feeling that those days are gone

                 forever, because we are going to watch a

                 champion in the second leg of the Triple

                 Crown.

                            Thank you, Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Nozzolio.

                            SENATOR NOZZOLIO:    Madam

                 President, on the resolution.

                            I rise with great pride in echoing

                 Senator Bruno's comments, our leader, who left

                 one important component out, that if it wasn't

                 for his leadership in establishing this entire

                 breeding industry and supporting it the way he

                 has, Senator, I daresay we all would not be as

                 successful here, not only with Funny Cide but

                 across the state.

                            I represent the Finger Lakes region

                 and the Finger Lakes Racetrack.  And I've

                 learned to be aware of the importance of

                 New York-bred thoroughbreds to the racing

                 industry and to our New York State economy.

                 Nearly 1200 New York bred horses are stabled



                                                        2458



                 at the Finger Lakes racetrack.  Nearly

                 80 percent of the races there are exclusively

                 for New York-breds.  And the track employs

                 over 1500 people on and off the track and

                 generates nearly $50 million in the activity

                 in our state economy.

                            And I say that because with one

                 swoop of the race, Funny Cide has done so much

                 to shed light on the importance of this very

                 important industry to New York State that I

                 rise to thank the owners and trainers and

                 congratulate them in echoing Senator Bruno's

                 comments.

                            That those buddies from Sackets

                 Harbor brought this courageous gelding to

                 victory, and that Funny Cide should be the

                 next "I Love New York" commercial.  Because to

                 see you on the winner's stand, the owners and

                 trainers and those who brought Funny Cide

                 there, our hearts were with such pride that

                 you brought this attention to such an

                 important industry in New York State.

                            I'd close by saying to Trainer Tagg

                 and Jack Knowlton and the rest of the partners

                 of Sackatoga Stables, yes, you won the Derby,



                                                        2459



                 we'll be rooting for you at the Preakness and

                 the Belmont stakes, but we really need you to

                 come to the Finger Lakes this year and win the

                 New York Derby at the track later this summer.

                            I can guarantee that the people of

                 the Finger Lakes region are very proud of what

                 you accomplished.  Thank you very, very much.

                 You've just added another chapter to why we

                 all love New York.

                            Thank you, Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Wright.

                            SENATOR WRIGHT:    Thank you, Madam

                 President.  On the resolution.

                            I stand to speak on behalf of the

                 other end of the state from Sackatoga.  That's

                 Sackets Harbor in Jefferson County.

                            Now, normally I'm rising from

                 Jefferson County to talks about dairy.  I

                 don't claim to have Leader Bruno's knowledge

                 of the horse industry.  But I do know some of

                 the individuals who have been involved and

                 invested in Sackatoga.  And we're very pleased

                 to see that investment come to fruition with

                 the winning of the Derby with Funny Cide.

                            Now, the history goes on that these



                                                        2460



                 gentlemen convened over some liquid

                 refreshment.  Now, those of you who don't know

                 where Sackets Harbor is, let me point out --

                 because it's been reported as Western New York

                 and many other things -- it's on the eastern

                 shore of Lake Ontario, one hour north of

                 Syracuse.  And it's home to Sackets Harbor

                 1812 beer, which is also bottled in Saratoga,

                 Senator Bruno's district.

                            So there are some very clear

                 correlations, many of which and many a good

                 idea in Sackets has started over a cold

                 refreshment.  Not the least of which was

                 Mr. Constance being elected mayor of the

                 village of Sackets Harbor.

                            (Laughter.)

                            SENATOR WRIGHT:    So he has spent

                 some time in our business as well.

                            But they truly are the pride of the

                 community.  The colors are the colors of the

                 local school district, the Sackets Harbor

                 School.  So you can see that there's a great

                 deal of pride.

                            We're very glad and very pleased to

                 have all of the owners that could join us



                                                        2461



                 today.  We want to extend congratulations on

                 behalf of Sackets Harbor, Jefferson County,

                 and those of us in the rest of the state who

                 are not as recognized as Saratoga.  Well done.

                            And Godspeed this weekend.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Farley.

                            SENATOR FARLEY:    Thank you, Madam

                 President.

                            I rise to pay tribute to this

                 magnificent team that put together a great

                 winner.  Having been born and raised in

                 Jefferson County and living in the summer a

                 lot in Sackets Harbor, my congratulations to

                 them.

                            But let me just say a word about

                 the Capital District and how we supported

                 Funny Cide.  The OTB parlors ran out of money.

                 They couldn't even pay off the bettors that

                 supported your horse.  And, you know, that

                 really says something.  And I'm sure there's

                 going to be a few bob waged this year in the

                 Preakness.

                            But we're very, very proud of you.

                 And as somebody that represents half of

                 Saratoga County -- usually the rural half.



                                                        2462



                 Senator Bruno gets all the famous people like

                 Funny Cide.  I get a few too.

                            But my congratulations to all the

                 owners, to Mrs. Santos.  There's wonderful

                 news coming on your husband, and we're very,

                 very proud of him.  What a great race.  And I

                 know he's going to be trying extra hard in

                 Preakness, and we're going to have a winner

                 come next Saturday.

                            All the best to everybody that's

                 involved with this great horse.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Hoffmann.

                            SENATOR HOFFMANN:    Thank you,

                 Madam President.

                            There are many of us here who look

                 upon this as a great victory, not only for the

                 horse world but for New York agriculture.  The

                 McMahons run a family farm.  And here in

                 New York State, we're very proud of the fact

                 that the number-two piece of agriculture in

                 our great agricultural heritage is the equine

                 world.  And with their great foresight and

                 success, we are now on the map.

                            The wonderful words that were

                 spoken in Kentucky were resounding all over



                                                        2463



                 the world.  And even today people are now

                 aware for the first time of New York's very

                 significant role in this industry.

                            In the 1970s, the foresight of some

                 of the people in this room that put together

                 the breeding fund has paid off handsomely.

                 And it is with the support of that breeders'

                 fund that we are able to continue building an

                 industry.

                            There are other states, other

                 countries that would only dare imagine what we

                 have here in New York State.  And yet so many

                 people in New York and other parts of the

                 United States have not fully grasped this

                 great wonder that we have in our breeding

                 industry.  With Funny Cide, now we have an

                 awareness.  And I think Senator Nozzolio said

                 it very effectively.  This is an "I Love New

                 York" campaign slogan absolutely packaged for

                 us.

                            Jack, when you said "This is one

                 for the little people," you were right.

                 Because we have small, very special farms as

                 well as large ones.  We have breeding programs

                 that include our SUNY campuses.  Morrisville



                                                        2464



                 University, right in the middle of my

                 district, has played a part in helping to

                 train some of the horses that have gone on to

                 great success.

                            This is a state where we all take

                 pride, and there are many ways that we are

                 going to continue growing this very

                 significant industry.

                            I'm proud of the fact that we've

                 taken the sales tax off of goods and purchases

                 that affect production agriculture, including

                 the equine world.  Let's see what we can do to

                 cheer this wonderful horse and his owners and

                 his trainers on to the next round.

                            Before I sit, I also have to say

                 it's unfortunate that there were people who

                 dared to question the way Funny Cide was

                 treated.  Because it is so well known that the

                 trainers of this magnificent horse have always

                 put the horse first.  That cannot be said for

                 every other horse and, indeed, for every other

                 state.

                            But here in New York, we take great

                 pride in the way all of our animals are

                 treated, and I'm proud of the fact that the



                                                        2465



                 owners and the trainers of Funny Cide have

                 always maintained the highest level of respect

                 for the animal.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator

                 Stachowski.

                            SENATOR STACHOWSKI:    I'd like to

                 rise also and join Senator Bruno in

                 congratulating the owners of Funny Cide and,

                 of course, Mrs. Santos, on behalf of her

                 husband, the jockey.

                            I think it's a great opportunity

                 for New York breeding to take another step

                 forward.  Obviously, now that you have a

                 New York-bred that's a Kentucky Derby winner,

                 that will help enormously.

                            And probably today, with everybody

                 so jubilant, would be a good time to look at

                 the way the breeders' fund is dealt with in

                 the OTB law.  And it might be a good time to

                 revisit that and make sure that the breeders'

                 fund and the breeders, the horse owners, get a

                 little bit better break out of OTB.

                            And maybe then they wouldn't have

                 so much money to buy racetracks and other

                 things, and they'd put the money into the



                                                        2466



                 breeding fund in New York State, where it

                 would be used much better by the people that

                 work so hard in this industry.  And obviously,

                 with this as a kick-off point, I can't see a

                 better time.

                            And I don't think that my talking

                 about this takes away anything from this

                 resolution, because the reason for this

                 resolution is to celebrate the fact that

                 New York State finally has a Kentucky Derby

                 winner.

                            And I'm not surprised that there

                 was a challenge about that, because I know

                 that in Kentucky, as happy as they are that

                 there was another great champion, they weren't

                 real happy that it was a New York-bred.

                 Because they always like the fact that it's a

                 Kentucky-bred horse or something of that

                 nature, and they don't like to see that spread

                 out.

                            And so it couldn't be a better day,

                 and I'm so happy for all the owners.  And

                 actually, due to my attending the dinner this

                 year and Howard Nolan introducing me to one of

                 the owners, it helped me out financially too,



                                                        2467



                 to have been at that dinner.

                            (Laughter.)

                            SENATOR STACHOWSKI:    So

                 congratulations, and good luck in the future.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Smith,

                 you wish to be heard?

                            SENATOR ADA SMITH:    Thank you,

                 Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    You're welcome.

                            SENATOR ADA SMITH:    I too rise to

                 congratulate the owners, the breeders, the

                 trainers, and especially our famous jockey.

                            I have to say that a few years ago

                 Senator Farley and I were here over the

                 weekend of the race, and we decided that we

                 would make a little wager.  And we won.

                            So the Friday before the race,

                 Senator Farley came to me and said:  "Are we

                 betting this year?"  And I hadn't paid any

                 attention to it.  So we got the paper, and

                 would you believe, I picked the horses in the

                 order that they won, the first three horses.

                            So I want to thank you for

                 benefiting me and my pocketbook.

                            (Laughter.)



                                                        2468



                            SENATOR ADA SMITH:    And I want to

                 thank you for being great sportspeople and for

                 bringing honor to the State of New York.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The question is

                 on the resolution.  All in favor please

                 signify by saying aye.

                            (Response of "Aye.")

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Opposed, nay.

                            (No response.)

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The resolution is

                 adopted.

                            And congratulations on behalf of

                 the Senate and the State of New York.

                            (Sustained applause.)

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Bruno.

                            SENATOR BRUNO:    Madam President,

                 can we at this time open this resolution to

                 all the members in the chamber.  And any that

                 would like not to be on it, just indicate

                 privately to the chair.

                            Thank you, Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Any member who

                 does not wish to sponsor this resolution

                 please notify the desk.

                            Senator Fuschillo.



                                                        2469



                            SENATOR FUSCHILLO:    Thank you,

                 Madam President.

                            On behalf of Senator LaValle, on

                 page number 32 I offer the following

                 amendments to Calendar Number 336, Senate

                 Print Number 281, and ask that said bill

                 retain its place on Third Reading Calendar.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The amendments

                 are received, and the bill will retain its

                 place on the Third Reading Calendar.

                            Senator Fuschillo.

                            SENATOR FUSCHILLO:    Madam

                 President, on behalf of Senator Larkin, on

                 page number 47 I offer the following

                 amendments to Calendar Number 592, Senate

                 Print Number 1222, and ask that said bill

                 retain its place on Third Reading Calendar.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The amendments

                 are received, and the bill will retain its

                 place on the Third Reading Calendar.

                            SENATOR FUSCHILLO:    Madam

                 President, on behalf of Senator Balboni, on

                 page number 42 I offer the following

                 amendments to Calendar Number 530, Senate

                 Print Number 3852, and ask that said bill



                                                        2470



                 retain its place on Third Reading Calendar.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The amendments

                 are received, and the bill will retain its

                 place on the Third Reading Calendar, Senator.

                            SENATOR FUSCHILLO:    Madam

                 President, on behalf of Senator Larkin, I wish

                 to call up Senate Print Number 1225, recalled

                 from the Assembly, which is now at the desk.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The Secretary

                 will read.

                            THE SECRETARY:    Calendar Number

                 108, by Senator Larkin, Senate Print 1225, an

                 act to amend the Civil Practice Law and Rules.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator

                 Fuschillo.

                            SENATOR FUSCHILLO:    Madam

                 President, I now move to reconsider the vote

                 by which the bill was passed.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The Secretary

                 will call the roll upon reconsideration.

                            (The Secretary called the roll.)

                            THE SECRETARY:    Ayes, 58.

                            SENATOR FUSCHILLO:    Madam

                 President, I now offer the following

                 amendments.



                                                        2471



                            THE PRESIDENT:    The amendments

                 are received, Senator.

                            Senator Schneiderman.

                            SENATOR SCHNEIDERMAN:    Thank you,

                 Madam President.

                            On behalf of Senator Parker, I

                 would move that the following bills be

                 discharged from their committees and be

                 recommitted with instructions to strike the

                 enacting clause:  Senate 4275, Senate 4277,

                            THE PRESIDENT:    So ordered,

                 Senator.

                            SENATOR SCHNEIDERMAN:    Thank you.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Velella.

                            SENATOR VELELLA:    Are there any

                 substitutions at the desk?

                 Senator.

                 Senator Maltese moves to discharge, from the

                 743.

                            On page 6, Senator Kuhl moves to

                 discharge, from the Committee on Local

                 ordered.

                 an act to repeal Title 17 of Article 23.
